## `app.api.crowd`

Source: [`backend/app/api/crowd.py`](../backend/app/api/crowd.py)

Routes for student crowd reports (not busy / moderate / crowded).

Calls services.crowd; no aggregation logic lives here. The current level for
every location is also in GET /locations and /locations/{id} (`crowd`).

### `get_throttle`

```python
def get_throttle() -> Throttle
```

The shared crowd-report throttle, as a dependency so tests can swap in a fresh one.

### `report_crowd`

```python
@router.post('/{location_id}', response_model=Crowd, status_code=201)
def report_crowd(location_id: int, report: CrowdReportIn, request: Request, db: Session=Depends(get_db), throttle: Throttle=Depends(get_throttle))
```

Report how busy a location is right now. Returns the location's crowd level after it.

One report per location per client every CROWD_REPORT_COOLDOWN_SECONDS (429 otherwise).

## `app.api.filters`

Source: [`backend/app/api/filters.py`](../backend/app/api/filters.py)

Routes for dietary filtering, single person and group.

Calls services.filter_engine; no filtering logic lives here. Profiles come in
the request body (POST) so dietary information never lands in URLs or logs,
and nothing about them is stored. One profile is the single-person case.

### `filter_menus`

```python
@router.post('/locations/{location_id}/menus', response_model=list[FilteredMenu])
def filter_menus(location_id: int, request: FilterRequest, on: date | None=Query(None, alias='date'), db: Session=Depends(get_db))
```

Every menu at a location on `date` (default today), each item checked against every profile.

### `filter_group`

```python
@router.post('/group', response_model=list[GroupLocation])
def filter_group(request: FilterRequest, at: datetime | None=None, db: Session=Depends(get_db))
```

Every location, ranked for a group: where everyone has something that fits on `at`'s day.

Order: locations where everyone fits first, then those open at `at`, then by name.

## `app.services.crowd`

Source: [`backend/app/services/crowd.py`](../backend/app/services/crowd.py)

Crowd aggregation.

Combines recent student reports into a crowd level per location.
Kept separate from filter_engine so the two features don't share a file.

Reports are only stored, never updated; the level is worked out here on
every read, so two students reporting at once can't corrupt it. Only reports
from the last CROWD_WINDOW_MINUTES count, and newer ones count more: a report
weighs 1 when new and falls linearly to 0 at the end of the window. No
reports in the window means the level is unknown (None), not "not busy".

### class `Crowd`

A location's crowd level from the reports in the window.

Fields:

- `level: str | None`
- `report_count: int`
- `last_reported_at: datetime | None`

### `aggregate`

```python
def aggregate(reports, at: datetime) -> Crowd
```

reports: (level, created_at) pairs for one location. Only those in (at - WINDOW, at] count.

### class `Throttle`

At most one report per key (client address + location) every `seconds`.

Kept in memory only, so no reporter data is stored. The API is a single
process, so one dict is enough; it resets on restart.

#### `hit`

```python
def hit(self, key) -> float
```

Record a report for key. Returns 0 if allowed, else seconds until it would be.

## `app.services.filter_engine`

Source: [`backend/app/services/filter_engine.py`](../backend/app/services/filter_engine.py)

```text
Dietary filter engine.

Checks menu items against one or more dietary profiles and labels each
result as fits, conflicts, or incomplete (data incomplete). Never treats
missing allergen data as safe. Pure functions, no database.

The rules, per profile (a wrong "fits" can hurt someone, so every gap in the
data makes a result incomplete, never fits):

Allergens the profile avoids
    the item lists one (icon, or its label's "Contains:")   conflicts
    the item has a trait or "Contains:" name we don't know  incomplete: it might be one
    the item has no nutrition label                         incomplete: icons alone may miss one
Diets the profile requires
    the item is tagged with it (vegan also counts as vegetarian)        fits
    the item lists an allergen the diet rules out (DIET_EXCLUDES)       conflicts
    otherwise                                                           incomplete: untagged
                                                                        doesn't prove either way
Goals (min protein, max calories, max sodium)
    no label, or the label doesn't give that nutrient       incomplete
    outside the limit                                       conflicts

Overall: any conflict -> conflicts, else any incomplete -> incomplete, else fits.
```

### class `Profile`

One person's dietary needs: allergens to avoid, required diets, and nutrition goals.

Fields:

- `avoid: frozenset[str]`
- `diets: frozenset[str]`
- `min_protein_g: float | None`
- `max_calories: float | None`
- `max_sodium_mg: float | None`

### class `Result`

One item's verdict for one profile (fits, conflicts, or incomplete), with reasons.

Fields:

- `verdict: str`
- `reasons: list[str]`

### `check`

```python
def check(item, profile: Profile) -> Result
```

One item against one profile.

item is anything with .allergens, .diets, .unrecognized_traits (lists) and
.nutrition (None, or something with .protein_g, .calories, .sodium_mg and
optionally .ingredient_flags, e.g. {"dairy": ["whey"]}).

### class `Counts`

How many items fit, are incomplete, or conflict for one profile.

Fields:

- `fits: int`
- `incomplete: int`
- `conflicts: int`

### `count`

```python
def count(items, profile: Profile) -> Counts
```

How many of a location's items fit, conflict, or are incomplete for one profile.

## `app.services.freshness`

Source: [`backend/app/services/freshness.py`](../backend/app/services/freshness.py)

How fresh the scraped data is.

The team scrapes by hand once a day, so data is stale once the last
completed run is older than STALE_AFTER_HOURS (default 36: a day plus slack
for a late run).

### `is_stale`

```python
def is_stale(last_finished_at: datetime | None, at: datetime) -> bool
```

True if there's no completed run, or the last one finished over STALE_AFTER_HOURS before `at`.

## `app.services.hours`

Source: [`backend/app/services/hours.py`](../backend/app/services/hours.py)

Opening hours: turn stored hours rows into times, and answer "open at T?".

Pure functions, no database. Ingestion stores one row per location and date
(db.models.HoursDay): status "open" / "closed" / "unknown", and windows as
[open_minute, close_minute] after that date's midnight. A close at or past
1440 runs into the next day, so "open at 12:30am" must also check the
previous day's row.

### `campus_time`

```python
def campus_time(at: datetime | None=None) -> datetime
```

`at` in campus time. None means now; a naive datetime is taken as campus time.

### `periods`

```python
def periods(day: date, windows: list) -> list[tuple[datetime, datetime]]
```

[[420, 1260]] on 2026-10-06 -> [(Oct 6 7:00am, Oct 6 9:00pm)], in campus time.

### class `OpenState`

Whether a location is open at a moment, and when it closes or next opens.

Fields:

- `is_open: bool | None`
- `closes_at: datetime | None`
- `opens_next_at: datetime | None`

### `open_state`

```python
def open_state(at: datetime, today, yesterday) -> OpenState
```

Whether a location is open at `at`.

today / yesterday are HoursDay rows (anything with .date, .status,
.windows) for at's date and the day before, or None if not stored.

## `app.services.label_reviews`

Source: [`backend/app/services/label_reviews.py`](../backend/app/services/label_reviews.py)

Apply approved label reviews (#18): remove diet tags a person confirmed are contradicted.

NC State's data in the database is never changed. Each menu item is returned as
a view with the approved tags taken out of `diets` and the reasons in
`diets_removed`, e.g. {"vegan": "ingredients list chicken"}. A decision only
applies to the exact ingredient text it was made on, so if NC State changes the
ingredients, the tags come back until someone reviews the new text.

dish_name and ingredients_hash must match ingestion/label_reviews.py (a test
checks this).

### `dish_name`

```python
def dish_name(name: str) -> str
```

How a dish is matched across menus: its name, lowercased, spaces collapsed.

### `ingredients_hash`

```python
def ingredients_hash(ingredients: str | None) -> str
```

Fingerprint of the ingredient text a decision was made on (sha256 hex).

### `reviewed`

```python
def reviewed(item, location_id: int, approved: Approved) -> SimpleNamespace
```

A read-only view of `item` with any approved diet tags removed.

### `reviewed_items`

```python
def reviewed_items(menu, approved: Approved) -> list[SimpleNamespace]
```

A menu's items in id order, each with approved reviews applied.

Source: [`db/models.py`](../db/models.py)

```text
Tables.

Single writer per table (proj_1b report, Figure 1):
    ingestion/  writes locations, hours_days, menus, menu_items, nutrition, ingest_runs,
                label_reviews
    backend/    reads those; writes only crowd_reports

Unknown stays unknown: a NULL nutrient or a missing label means "not published",
never zero or safe.
```

### class `Base` (DeclarativeBase)

Base class for every table below. Its metadata lists them all, for Alembic.

### class `Location` (Base)

A NetNutrition dining unit. Writer: ingestion.

Fields:

- `id: Mapped[int]`
- `name: Mapped[str]`
- `description: Mapped[str | None]`
- `dining_slug: Mapped[str | None]`
- `updated_at: Mapped[datetime]`
- `menus: Mapped[list['Menu']]`

### class `HoursDay` (Base)

Hours for one location on one date, from dining.ncsu.edu. Writer: ingestion.

status is 'open', 'closed' (the site said "Closed all day"), or 'unknown'.
windows is a list of [open_minute, close_minute] after midnight; a close at or
past 1440 means the location closes at or after midnight.

Fields:

- `location_id: Mapped[int]`
- `date: Mapped[date]`
- `status: Mapped[str]`
- `windows: Mapped[list]`
- `raw_text: Mapped[str | None]`
- `fetched_at: Mapped[datetime]`

### class `Menu` (Base)

One meal on one day at one location. Writer: ingestion.

Fields:

- `id: Mapped[int]`
- `location_id: Mapped[int]`
- `date: Mapped[date]`
- `meal: Mapped[str]`
- `fetched_at: Mapped[datetime | None]`
- `location: Mapped[Location]`
- `items: Mapped[list['MenuItem']]`

### class `Nutrition` (Base)

One nutrition label. Writer: ingestion.

key is "<location_id>|<name>|<serving size>" (lowercased): the same dish at the
same location is fetched once and re-fetched when older than the cache limit.
Scoped per location because two halls can serve different recipes under one name.

Fields:

- `key: Mapped[str]`
- `location_id: Mapped[int]`
- `source_detail_oid: Mapped[int]`
- `serving_size: Mapped[str | None]`
- `calories: Mapped[float | None]`
- `protein_g: Mapped[float | None]`
- `fat_g: Mapped[float | None]`
- `carbs_g: Mapped[float | None]`
- `sodium_mg: Mapped[float | None]`
- `nutrients_raw: Mapped[dict]`
- `ingredients: Mapped[str | None]`
- `contains: Mapped[list]`
- `missing_fields: Mapped[list]`
- `ingredient_flags: Mapped[dict]`
- `fetched_at: Mapped[datetime]`

### class `MenuItem` (Base)

One dish on one menu. Writer: ingestion (replaced wholesale on each scrape).

allergens = the item's icon traits plus its label's "Contains:" list.
unrecognized_traits holds any icon or "Contains:" name we have no key for; the
filter engine must treat a non-empty list as "data incomplete", not as safe.
nutrition_key is NULL when no label was fetched or it failed verification.

Fields:

- `id: Mapped[int]`
- `menu_id: Mapped[int]`
- `detail_oid: Mapped[int]`
- `name: Mapped[str]`
- `course: Mapped[str | None]`
- `serving_size: Mapped[str | None]`
- `traits_raw: Mapped[list]`
- `allergens: Mapped[list]`
- `diets: Mapped[list]`
- `unrecognized_traits: Mapped[list]`
- `nutrition_key: Mapped[str | None]`
- `menu: Mapped[Menu]`
- `nutrition: Mapped[Nutrition | None]`

### class `IngestRun` (Base)

One run of the ingestion job: status, options, stats, errors. Writer: ingestion.

The API can read the latest row to show how fresh the data is.

Fields:

- `id: Mapped[int]`
- `started_at: Mapped[datetime]`
- `finished_at: Mapped[datetime | None]`
- `status: Mapped[str]`
- `options: Mapped[dict]`
- `stats: Mapped[dict]`
- `errors: Mapped[list]`

### class `CrowdReport` (Base)

One student's report of how busy a location is. Writer: backend (the API).

Append-only: the API never updates a row, and the crowd level is computed from
recent rows on read, so two reports at once can't race. Nothing about the
reporter is stored.

Fields:

- `id: Mapped[int]`
- `location_id: Mapped[int]`
- `level: Mapped[str]`
- `created_at: Mapped[datetime]`

### class `LabelReview` (Base)

A diet tag that NC State's own ingredients contradict, for a person to decide.
Writer: ingestion (the scraper adds pending rows; the review command decides).

A dish is a location plus its name (NetNutrition gives it a new item id on
every menu). ingredients_hash pins the decision to the ingredient text it was
made on: if NC State changes the ingredients, a new review is needed.
Approved rows tell the API to remove `tags` from the dish; NC State's own
data in menu_items is never changed.

Fields:

- `id: Mapped[int]`
- `location_id: Mapped[int]`
- `dish: Mapped[str]`
- `item_name: Mapped[str]`
- `tags: Mapped[list]`
- `words: Mapped[list]`
- `ingredients_hash: Mapped[str]`
- `status: Mapped[str]`
- `first_seen_at: Mapped[datetime]`
- `decided_at: Mapped[datetime | None]`
- `decided_by: Mapped[str | None]`
- `reason: Mapped[str | None]`

## `ingestion.backfill_flags`

Source: [`ingestion/backfill_flags.py`](../ingestion/backfill_flags.py)

```text
Recompute nutrition.ingredient_flags from the ingredient text already stored.

Labels are only re-fetched every LABEL_MAX_AGE_DAYS, so labels saved before the
column existed (or before a word-list change) keep old flags until then. This
recomputes them from the stored text. No requests to NC State.

Usage (from proj_2/, with DATABASE_URL set and migrations applied):
    python -m ingestion.backfill_flags           preview: how many labels would change
    python -m ingestion.backfill_flags --write   save the new flags

Takes the ingestion lock, so it never runs during a scrape.
```

```python
def backfill(engine: Engine, write: bool) -> dict
```

Returns {"labels": checked, "changed": would change or did change}.


```text
Discrepancy report: labels whose ingredients name an allergen NC State's label leaves out.

Read-only. One row per label (dishes share labels), for items on menus between
--start and --end, as CSV for NC State Dining to check:
- an allergen the ingredients mention that isn't in the item's allergens, or
- an item tagged vegetarian/vegan whose ingredients mention something that diet
  rules out.
A row is a possible label gap, not a confirmed one: a person should check it.

Usage (from proj_2/, with DATABASE_URL set):
    python -m ingestion.discrepancy_report --start 2026-10-19 --end 2026-10-25 > report.csv
```

## `ingestion.fetch`

Source: [`ingestion/fetch.py`](../ingestion/fetch.py)

```text
Fetch: the only code that talks to the network.

Polite by design: one request at a time, at least REQUEST_DELAY_SECONDS apart,
an identifying User-Agent, and backed-off retries only for errors worth retrying.

NetNutrition is stateful. The first GET sets an ASP.NET session cookie, and every
click after that is a POST to <page>/<Controller>/<Action> (see the site's own
Scripts/cbord_nn_ui_repsonsive.js) answering
    {"success": true, "panels": [{"id": "menuPanel", "html": "..."}, ...]}
The server remembers the selected unit and menu, so calls must run in order:
select unit -> select menu -> labels for that menu. Never parallelize a session.
```

A request failed, or a page wasn't what the scraper expected.

## `ingestion.ingredients`

Source: [`ingestion/ingredients.py`](../ingestion/ingredients.py)

Possible allergens: what an item's ingredient text mentions.

NC State's icons and "Contains:" line sometimes leave out an allergen the
ingredients name (M0 eval, issue #15). This scan finds those words so the filter
can mark the item "incomplete" instead of "fits". A hit is only a possibility,
never a confirmed allergen: it is stored apart from NC State's allergens.

Deterministic: the same text always gives the same sorted keys. Matching is
whole words, any case, with an optional plural "s"/"es".

Sources for each key are noted next to its words. Cross-contact warnings ("may
contain", "made in a facility that also processes ...") are not ingredients and
are ignored. Halal is not scanned beyond pork: there is no single standard for
it (certifiers differ on alcohol and gelatin sources).

The words started from eval/wordlist.py but are kept here on purpose, so the M0
eval stays an independent check of this scan.

### `matched_terms`

```python
def matched_terms(ingredients: str | None) -> dict[str, list[str]]
```

Each key the ingredient text mentions, with the listed words that matched.

{"dairy": ["whey"]} lets the app say "ingredients mention whey". Keys and
words are sorted; {} if nothing matched or there is no text.

### `possible_allergens`

```python
def possible_allergens(ingredients: str | None) -> list[str]
```

Keys the ingredient text mentions, sorted. [] if none or no text.

## `ingestion.label_reviews`

Source: [`ingestion/label_reviews.py`](../ingestion/label_reviews.py)

Label reviews: find diet tags that an item's own ingredients contradict (#18).

After each scrape, every item tagged vegan, vegetarian, or halal is checked
against its label's ingredients. A contradiction becomes a `pending` row in
label_reviews for a person to approve or reject. One row per dish and
ingredient text: a repeat scrape adds nothing, and new ingredient text needs a
new decision.

The diet rules follow the sources in ingestion/ingredients.py (Vegetarian
Society, Vegan Society; pork for halal) and match DIET_DOUBTED_BY in
backend/app/services/filter_engine.py.

### `dish_name`

```python
def dish_name(name: str) -> str
```

How a dish is matched across menus: its name, lowercased, spaces collapsed.

### `ingredients_hash`

```python
def ingredients_hash(ingredients: str | None) -> str
```

Fingerprint of the ingredient text a decision is made on (sha256 hex).

### `contradictions`

```python
def contradictions(diets: list[str], ingredients: str | None) -> dict[str, list[str]]
```

Diet tags the ingredients contradict, with the words why: {"vegan": ["chicken"]}.

### `record`

```python
def record(db: Session, start: date, end: date, now: datetime) -> tuple[int, int]
```

Add pending reviews for contradicted items on scraped menus from start to end.

Returns (new reviews added, reviews pending in total). The caller commits.

Allergens, diets, and unrecognized names for one item.

## `ingestion.run`

Source: [`ingestion/run.py`](../ingestion/run.py)

```text
Run the ingestion job once: Fetch -> Parse -> Normalize + Label -> Write.

Usage (from proj_2/, with DATABASE_URL set and migrations applied):
    python -m ingestion.run                        all units, 7 days, with nutrition labels
    python -m ingestion.run --units 1 --days 1     Fountain, today only
    python -m ingestion.run --no-nutrition         menus + icon traits only (fast)

Every run leaves an ingest_runs row with its options, stats, and errors. A failure in
one unit or menu is recorded and the job moves on; a failure of the whole job is
recorded as status 'failed'. Only one run at a time (Postgres advisory lock).
```


Delete this location's menus dated within the listed range that the site no longer lists.

Only the listed date range is touched, so past menus are kept, and an empty list
deletes nothing (we can't tell "removed" from "page didn't load").

### `upsert_nutrition`

```python
def upsert_nutrition(db: Session, location_id: int, detail_oid: int, row: ItemRow, label: Label) -> list[str]
```

Store a verified label under the item's cache key; returns its "Contains:" list.

### `replace_menu_items`

```python
def replace_menu_items(db: Session, menu_id: int, location_id: int, rows: list[ItemRow], contains_by_key: dict[str, list[str]]) -> str
```

Replace a menu's items. Returns 'new', 'changed', or 'same' versus the last scrape.

contains_by_key maps nutrition keys to the "Contains:" list of a stored label;
items whose key is absent get no nutrition link and only their icon allergens.

# M0 eval: `eval/`

## `eval`

Source: [`eval/__init__.py`](../eval/__init__.py)

M0 risk-killer eval (see docs/m0-eval.md).

The eval runs PackPlate's real filter engine, which lives in backend/app, so
backend/ goes on the import path here. That keeps the one command,
`python -m eval.m0` from proj_2/, working without extra setup.

## `eval.baseline`

Source: [`eval/baseline.py`](../eval/baseline.py)

The icon-only baseline M0 compares PackPlate against.

It filters the way NetNutrition's own trait filter does: it reads only the
icons on the menu. Avoiding an allergen, an item is out only if it shows that
allergen's icon; no icon counts as safe, even with no nutrition label, an
"Unknown" trait, or the allergen listed only in the label's "Contains:" line.
Requiring a diet, an item fits only if it carries that diet's icon, with the
same rule as PackPlate (vegan also counts as vegetarian), so the comparison
isolates how missing allergen data is handled.

There is no "incomplete": every answer is fits or conflicts.

### `check`

```python
def check(icons: list[str], profile: Profile) -> str
```

One item, given its icon titles as published, against one profile.

## `eval.export_snapshot`

Source: [`eval/export_snapshot.py`](../eval/export_snapshot.py)

```text
Export the frozen M0 snapshot from the database, trimmed to what the eval needs.

The days are fixed in the M0 pre-registration issue: the first three weekdays
of the latest full scrape. Run once, from proj_2/, with DATABASE_URL set:

    python -m eval.export_snapshot

It only reads. It writes eval/data/snapshot.json; the eval reads only that
file, never the database, so anyone can reproduce its numbers.
```

### `to_snapshot`

```python
def to_snapshot(locations, hours, menus, days) -> dict
```

Plain, sorted data from database rows (or anything with the same fields).

Labels are stored once and items point to them by key. Menus that were
listed but never scraped (no items) are left out. Hours include the day
before the first day, because late hours can run past midnight.

### `summary`

```python
def summary(snapshot: dict) -> dict
```

Counts worth eyeballing after an export.

### `main`

```python
def main()
```

Read the snapshot days from the database and write eval/data/snapshot.json.

## `eval.m0`

Source: [`eval/m0.py`](../eval/m0.py)

```text
M0 risk-killer eval: is PackPlate safe, and is it useful? One command, from proj_2/:

    python -m eval.m0            # compute, print, and write eval/results.json
    python -m eval.m0 --check    # recompute and fail if it differs from results.json

Inputs, all committed: the frozen snapshot, the hand spot-check sheet, and the
simulation settings. Thresholds were posted in the pre-registration issue
before the first run. A missed threshold is reported, not an error: only a
crash, a stale spot-check sheet, or (with --check) a changed result fails.

Safe: every `fits` answer was scanned against its ingredient list; a person
read every flag (and 30 random unflagged answers). Confirmed flags are false
fits, counted separately for PackPlate and the icon-only baseline.

Useful: a simulated group is answered if some location is open at the group's
time and every person has at least one `fits` item on that meal's menu (or an
all-day menu). Unknown hours count as closed: we can't promise it's open.
```

### class `StaleSheet` (Exception)

Raises StaleSheet if a decision is missing or isn't allowed for its row kind.

The filled sheet must cover exactly the rows the scan produces today.

The Safe numbers: confirmed false fits per filter, and how the scan did.

Whether `item` fits `profile` under `which` filter: "packplate" or "baseline".

Of every item x test profile, the share PackPlate holds back as incomplete.

## `eval.profiles`

Source: [`eval/profiles.py`](../eval/profiles.py)

The eleven M0 test profiles, as fixed in the pre-registration issue:
one per allergen PackPlate knows and one per diet.

## `eval.scan`

Source: [`eval/scan.py`](../eval/scan.py)

```text
Ingredient scan: does an item's ingredient text name something a profile avoids?

This is M0's independent safety check. PackPlate's filter never reads
ingredient text (it uses the icons and the label's "Contains:" line), so a
`fits` item whose ingredients name an avoided allergen is a lead worth a
human look. The words are in eval/wordlist.py.

Two kinds of hit are kept apart:
- `terms`: words in the ingredients themselves.
- `advisory`: words only inside a cross-contact warning ("may contain",
  "made in a facility that also processes ..."). Those aren't ingredients,
  so they're reported separately, not counted as false fits.
```

### class `Hits`

The words the scan found: in the ingredients, and only in warnings.

Fields:

- `terms: list[str]`
- `advisory: list[str]`

### `term_pattern`

```python
def term_pattern(term: str) -> re.Pattern
```

Whole words, any case, optional plural; "half and half" also matches hyphens.

### `scan`

```python
def scan(ingredients: str | None, profile_key: str) -> Hits
```

Words in `ingredients` that break the profile, split by where they appear.

## `eval.simulate`

Source: [`eval/simulate.py`](../eval/simulate.py)

Simulated groups for M0's "Useful" claim. These are simulated users, not real ones.

Each group is 2-5 people at one of the snapshot's mealtimes. Each person
independently gets each allergy (and halal) with the probability in
eval/simulation.json, and one diet: vegan, vegetarian, or none. Most people end up
with no restriction at all, as in real life. A fixed seed makes the same groups
every run.

### class `Group`

One simulated group: when and at which meal they eat, and each person's needs.

Fields:

- `at: datetime`
- `meal: str`
- `people: tuple[Profile, ...]`

### `load_config`

```python
def load_config(path: Path=CONFIG) -> dict
```

The simulation settings in eval/simulation.json.

### `person`

```python
def person(rng: random.Random, config: dict) -> Profile
```

One simulated person, drawn with the probabilities in `config`.

### `groups`

```python
def groups(config: dict) -> list[Group]
```

All the simulated groups. The same seed always gives the same groups.

## `eval.spot_check`

Source: [`eval/spot_check.py`](../eval/spot_check.py)

```text
Build the hand spot-check sheet: every scan flag, plus 30 random unflagged items.

Run once, from proj_2/:

    python -m eval.spot_check

It writes eval/data/spot_check.csv for a person to fill in, and refuses to
overwrite a sheet that already exists, so filled-in decisions can't be lost.

One row per recipe (nutrition label) per test profile: the same dish on many
menus is read once. Only items that come out `fits` under PackPlate or the
icon-only baseline are scanned, since only those can be false fits.

The `decision` column:
- flagged rows: "confirm" (a real false fit) or "reject" (the word misfired)
- sample rows: "ok" (nothing avoided in the ingredients) or "missed" (the scan
  missed something)
```

### `context`

```python
def context(ingredients: str, terms: list[str], width: int=40) -> str
```

The text around every place each matched word appears, to read at a glance.

Shows every occurrence, including ones an exception removed before matching
("cocoa butter"), so the reviewer sees all of them and judges the real one.

### `candidates`

```python
def candidates(snapshot: dict) -> list[dict]
```

Every (recipe, profile) that fits under either filter, with its scan hits.

### `sheet`

```python
def sheet(rows: list[dict], sample_size: int=SAMPLE_SIZE, seed: int=SEED)
```

Flagged rows first, then a fixed random sample of scannable unflagged rows.

Flagged rows are sorted by matched word and context, so identical cases
(one shared sauce in many recipes) sit next to each other.

### `main`

```python
def main()
```

Write eval/data/spot_check.csv, unless a sheet already exists.

## `eval.wordlist`

Source: [`eval/wordlist.py`](../eval/wordlist.py)

```text
Ingredient words that mean an item breaks a test profile. Reviewed by a human.

For each test profile: `terms` that flag an item, and `except_` phrases that are
removed before matching because they look like a term but aren't one (cocoa
butter isn't dairy). Matching ignores case, needs whole words, and also matches
a plural "s" / "es". A flag is only a lead: a person confirms or rejects every
one in the spot-check.

Deliberately left out, and listed as limits in the results:
- "natural flavors", "spices", "seasoning": can hide an allergen, but the text
  doesn't say which.
- coconut: not counted as a nut here; NC State's "Contains Nuts" covers peanuts
  and tree nuts and doesn't say how it treats coconut.
- oats: often contaminated with gluten, but not a gluten ingredient.
- vanilla extract and other flavor extracts: contain alcohol, but whether that
  matters for halal is disputed.
- Meat that isn't pork can't be shown to be non-halal from ingredients.
```
